record.paper_title: Some Open Problems of Ramsey Minimal Graphs
record.original_question: For each integer n ≥ 6, characterize all graphs F that are Ramsey (2K₂, Pₙ)-minimal; that is, every red-blue coloring of the edges of F contains either a red copy of 2K₂ or a blue copy of Pₙ, but for every edge e of F the graph F − e has some red-blue coloring with neither a red copy of 2K₂ nor a blue copy of Pₙ.

evidence.quote: say that \(F \rightarrow (G, H)\) if whenever the edges of \(F\) are 2-colored, say with red and blue, there is either a red copy of \(G\) or a blue copy of \(H\). A graph \(F\) is called Ramsey \((G, H)\)-minimal if \(F \rightarrow (G, H)\) but for any edge \(e \in E(F)\), we have \((F - e) \nrightarrow (G, H)\).
More specifically, these problems consider the case where \(G = 2K\_{2}\), the matching on 2 edges.

evidence.page: zbMATH review body, Problem 2 second clause
evidence.quote: For each \(n \geq 6\), characterize the graphs in \(\mathfrak{R}(2K\_{2}, P\_{n})\).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $2K_2$ denote the graph consisting of two disjoint edges, and for an integer $n\ge 2$ let $P_n$ denote the path on $n$ vertices. For graphs $G$ and $H$, write $F\to (G,H)$ if every red–blue coloring of the edges of $F$ contains either a red subgraph isomorphic to $G$ or a blue subgraph isomorphic to $H$. A graph $F$ is called Ramsey $(G,H)$-minimal if $F\to (G,H)$ and, for every edge $e\in E(F)$, $F-e\not\to (G,H)$. Let $\mathcal R(G,H)$ denote the class of all Ramsey $(G,H)$-minimal graphs (up to isomorphism).

Problem: For each integer $n\ge 6$, give a complete characterization of the graphs in $\mathcal R(2K_2,P_n)$.
artifact.status_search_result: Complete characterizations of $\mathcal R(2K_2,P_n)$ are known only for small $n$ (notably $n=4,5$ by Baskoro and Yulianti, and partial structural results for general $n$, e.g., that $2P_n$ is the unique disconnected member and no tree belongs to the class). No reference found that provides a full characterization for $n\ge 6$, so the problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Ramsey minimal graphs for 2K2 versus Pn
status_evidence.snippet: Studies members of R(2K_2, P_n); 2P_n is the only disconnected graph in this set and no tree is a member; characterization for n=4,5 by Baskoro and Yulianti.
status_evidence.claim: Only partial structural results and characterizations for n=4,5 are available.

status_evidence.title: On Ramsey (2K2, Wn)-minimal graphs of smallest order
status_evidence.snippet: References Baskoro–Yulianti characterization of R(2K_2, P_n) for n in {3,4,5}; later n cases not characterized.
status_evidence.claim: Full characterization of R(2K_2, P_n) for n>=6 is not stated in the literature, indicating the problem remains open.
